Decoupling-Cap PDN Impedance
The board in `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb` has a 3V3 rail and one existing 100 nF decoupling capacitor. `/home/user/Desktop/target_z.csv` gives the maximum impedance at five frequencies, and `/home/user/Desktop/cap_models.csv` gives each available capacitor's C, ESR, and ESL.

For every capacitor, including the original one, use `Zc = ESR + j*(2*pi*f*ESL - 1/(2*pi*f*C))`. Combine all six capacitors by summed admittance, `Z_total = 1 / sum(1/Zc)`. Do not add source, plane, mounting, or other parasitics beyond the listed ESR and ESL. Add capacitors until this model meets every target and record the resulting magnitude `abs(Z_total)`.

Requirements: `/home/user/Desktop/pdn_analysis.csv` has exactly five data rows with columns `freq_hz,z_ohm`, and every `z_ohm` is at or below the matching target. The final board has exactly six capacitor footprints including the original; every value is listed in cap_models.csv; each capacitor is within 5 mm center-to-center of a 3V3 pad, inside the (0,0)-(80,60) outline, and does not overlap another footprint. Write `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb` and `/home/user/Desktop/pdn_analysis.csv`. [Software] Use KiCad 10.0.2; run `kicad` for the GUI or `kicad-cli` for scripting/headless use (use PATH or the full install path).
